source.note: Scan without a text layer. Unlike the 2025 papers the PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 14); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover also mentions a 23-page special answer book, which is not in this PDF. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 300 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md: Truck drivers travel a certain distance and have a rest before travelling further. A driver kept record of the distance he travelled (in km) on 8 trips and the amount of time he rested (in minutes) before he continued his journey. The information is given in the table below.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of the least squares regression line for the data.
If a truck driver travelled 550 km, predict the amount of time (in minutes) that he should rest before continuing his journey.
Write down the correlation coefficient for the data.
Interpret your answer to QUESTION 1.3.

questions.stem_md: At each stop, the truck driver spent money buying food and other refreshments. The amount spent (in rands) is given in the table below.

table.caption: Amount spent (in rands) at each stop

questions.text_md: Calculate the mean amount of money he spent at each stop.
Calculate the standard deviation for the data.
At how many stops did the driver spend an amount that was less than one standard deviation below the mean?

questions.stem_md: At a certain school, the staff committee wanted to determine how many glasses of water the staff members drank during a school day. All teachers present on a specific day were interviewed. The information is shown in the table below.

header: NUMBER OF GLASSES OF WATER DRANK PER DAY

questions.text_md: Complete the cumulative frequency column provided in the table in the ANSWER BOOK.
questions.notes: The task is to build the cumulative frequency column from the class frequencies (the reverse of stat.frequency-from-cumulative); no closer skill exists.

questions.text_md: How many staff members were interviewed?
How many staff members drank fewer than 6 glasses of water during a school day?

The staff committee observed that $k$ teachers were absent on the day of the interviews. It was found that half of these $k$ teachers drank from 0 to fewer than 2 (that is $0\leq x<2$) glasses of water per day, while the remainder of them drank from 4 to fewer than 6 (that is $4\leq x<6$) glasses of water per day. When these $k$ teachers are included in the data, the estimated mean is $4$ glasses of water per staff member per day.

How many teachers were absent on the day of the interviews?

questions.stem_md: In the figure, L$(-4\,;\,1)$, S$(4\,;\,5)$ and N$(-2\,;\,-3)$ are the vertices of a triangle having $S\hat{L}N=90^{\circ}$. LN intersects the $x$-axis at K.

questions.text_md: Calculate the length of SL. Leave your answer in surd form.
Calculate the gradient of SN.
Calculate the size of $\theta$, the angle of inclination of SN.
Calculate the size of $L\hat{N}S$.
Determine the equation of the line which passes through L and is parallel to SN. Write your answer in the form $y=mx+c$.
Calculate the area of $\triangle$LSN.
questions.notes: No dedicated coordinate-geometry area skill; tagged with ageo.distance-formula (the triangle is right-angled at L, so the area is $\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\mathrm{SL}\cdot\mathrm{LN}$).

questions.text_md: Calculate the coordinates of point P, which is equidistant from L, S and N.
Calculate the size of $L\hat{P}S$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, the circle with centre O has the equation $x^{2}+y^{2}=20$. G$(t\,;\,0)$ is the centre of the larger circle. A common tangent touches the circles at D and F respectively, such that D$(p\,;\,-2)$ lies in the $4^{\text{th}}$ quadrant.

questions.text_md: Given that D$(p\,;\,-2)$ lies on the smaller circle, show that $p=4$.
E$(6\,;\,2)$ is the midpoint of DF. Determine the coordinates of F.
Determine the equation of the common tangent, DF, in the form $y=mx+c$.
Calculate the value of $t$. Show ALL working.
Determine the equation of the larger circle in the form $ax^{2}+by^{2}+cx+dy+e=0$.
The smaller circle must be translated by $k$ units along the $x$-axis to touch the larger circle internally. Calculate the possible values of $k$.

questions.stem_md:
Given: $\sin\beta=\dfrac{1}{3}$, where $\beta\in(90^{\circ}\,;\,270^{\circ})$

**Without using a calculator, determine each of the following:**

questions.text_md: $\cos\beta$
$\sin 2\beta$
$\cos(450^{\circ}-\beta)$
Prove that $\dfrac{\cos^{4}x+\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}{1+\sin x}=1-\sin x$
For what value(s) of $x$ in the interval $x\in[0^{\circ}\,;\,360^{\circ}]$ is $\dfrac{\cos^{4}x+\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}{1+\sin x}$ undefined?
Write down the minimum value of the function defined by $y=\dfrac{\cos^{4}x+\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}{1+\sin x}$
Use the above identity to deduce that $\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B$
Hence, or otherwise, determine the general solution of the equation $\sin 48^{\circ}\cos x-\cos 48^{\circ}\sin x=\cos 2x$
Simplify $\dfrac{\sin 3x+\sin x}{\cos 2x+1}$ to a single trigonometric ratio.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, the graphs of $f(x)=2\sin 2x$ and $g(x)=-\cos(x+45^{\circ})$ are drawn for the interval $x\in[0^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$. A$(105^{\circ}\,;\,-1)$ lies on $f$.

questions.text_md: Write down the period of $f$.
Determine the range of $g$ in the interval $x\in[0^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$.

questions.stem_md: Determine the values of $x$, in the interval $x\in[0^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$, for which:

questions.text_md: $f(x)\cdot g(x)>0$
Another graph $p$ is defined as $p(x)=-f(x)$. D$(k\,;\,-1)$ lies on $p$. Determine the value(s) of $k$ in the interval $x\in[0^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for a reflection in the $x$-axis; tagged with fn.translate-graph as the closest transformation skill.

questions.text_md: Graph $h$ is obtained when $g$ is translated $45^{\circ}$ to the left. Determine the equation of $h$. Write your answer in its simplest form.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, S, T and K lie in the same horizontal plane. RS is a vertical tower. The angle of depression from R to K is $\beta$. $T\hat{S}K=\alpha$, TS $=p$ metres and the area of $\triangle$STK is $q$ m$^{2}$.

questions.text_md: Determine the length of SK in terms of $p$, $q$ and $\alpha$.
Show that $\mathrm{RS}=\dfrac{2q\tan\beta}{p\sin\alpha}$
Calculate the size of $\alpha$ if $\alpha<90^{\circ}$ and RS $=70$ m, $p=80$ m, $q=2\,500$ m$^{2}$ and $\beta=42^{\circ}$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, O is the centre of the circle.
questions.text_md: Use the diagram above to prove the theorem which states that the angle subtended by a chord at the centre of the circle is equal to twice the angle subtended by the same chord at the circumference, that is, prove that $T\hat{O}P=2T\hat{K}P$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, O is the centre of the circle and ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. OB and OD are drawn.
questions.text_md: If $\hat{O}_{1}=4x+100^{\circ}$ and $\hat{C}=x+34^{\circ}$, calculate, giving reasons, the size of $x$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, O is the centre of the larger circle. OB is a diameter of the smaller circle. Chord AB of the larger circle intersects the smaller circle at M and B.

questions.text_md: Write down the size of $O\hat{M}B$. Provide a reason.
If AB $=\sqrt{300}$ units and OM $=5$ units, calculate, giving reasons, the length of OB.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, ABCD is a parallelogram with AB $=14$ units. AD is produced to E such that AD $:$ DE $=4:3$. EB intersects DC in F. EB $=21$ units.

questions.text_md: Calculate, with reasons, the length of FB.
Prove, with reasons, that $\triangle$EDF $|||$ $\triangle$EAB.
Calculate, with reasons, the length of FC.
